answer: A mechanism that actually bites: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because echo only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, island is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any juniper approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
